subject: EVALUATE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB396.md — ALL FOUR recorded divergences are closed, and each was re-measured on this tree rather than inherited. (1) range-expression's trailing [ IN alphabet-name-1 ]: `valueRange : valueOperand (THRU|THROUGH) valueOperand (IN cobolWord)?` — `EVALUATE WS-C WHEN "A" THRU "M" IN MY-ALPHA` now runs (probe fmt_rest.cob prints RANGE-IN-ALPHA). (2) partial-expression-1: `evaluateWhenItem` carries `| partialExpression` — `EVALUATE WS-N WHEN > 5` now runs (same probe, PARTIAL-GT5). Those two were closed by earlier landings; re-probed here because a note's word is not evidence. (3) imperative-statement-1 sits INSIDE the outer brace group, unbracketed, so §5.2.6.3 makes it required and §5.2.6.2 gives the omission licence to brackets only: `evaluateWhenClause` now reads `evaluateWhenPhrase+ statementBlock` (statementBlock IS statement+), and `EVALUATE X WHEN 3 END-EVALUATE` is refused COBOL2072 where it used to compile in silence. The outer `{ … } …` is itself unbracketed, so at least one ordinary WHEN group is required and an EVALUATE whose only clause is WHEN OTHER is no longer a spelling of this statement. (4) `[ WHEN OTHER imperative-statement-2 ]` is ONE bracketed phrase FOLLOWING the repetition — §5.2.7 scopes an ellipsis to the portion between the delimiters immediately to its left, which the OTHER phrase is outside of — so it is a trailing `evaluateWhenOther?` on `evaluateStatement` rather than a second alternative of the repeated clause. A repeated or mispositioned WHEN OTHER is refused COBOL2073; it used to be admitted at any position any number of times, with EvaluateBinder's `other = body` discarding all but the last. The positive control at the introducing edition writes every position WITH its imperative and pins the values from the general rules, so the tightening cannot have been "satisfied" by refusing the construct. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolControlFlow.g4#evaluateWhenGroup (kb/Work PB2722 deleted the evaluateWhenGroup rule (its NOT? moved onto the five selection-object alternatives of evaluateWhenItem that print it) and renamed the arity fact to WhenPhrase_HoldsExactlyOneSelectionObjectPerPosition) retired-witness: unit:EvaluateSelectionObjectArityDriftTests.WhenGroup_HoldsExactlyOneSelectionObject (kb/Work PB2722 deleted the evaluateWhenGroup rule (its NOT? moved onto the five selection-object alternatives of evaluateWhenItem that print it) and renamed the arity fact to WhenPhrase_HoldsExactlyOneSelectionObjectPerPosition) Re-affirmed 2026-10-22 (kb/Work PB3530) against the figure regenerated from the printed page: render_figure.py's brace-group layout now keeps every alternative inside its own enclosure, so the diagram's layout changed while its words did not (sweep_figures.py's word gate); the verdict stands on the printed format.
